verdict.rationale: Both refactors keep the original order of side effects, error messages, statuses and exception chaining, so behavior is preserved in each. B also adds characterization tests that it ran against the old code. They cover the VIP stacking, shipping-threshold, rounding, invalid-coupon, partial-rollback and receipt-failure paths that the existing tests skip. For a refactor of live production code, this is the safety net a reviewer wants. A only ran the existing 9 tests and passed the coverage check on to the developer.
a_issues: No tests added, even though the existing suite skips the VIP, invalid-coupon, partial-rollback, free-shipping and receipt-failure paths of a production-critical function.
`_charge` signature is crammed onto one very long line.
Uses a bare `list` type for reserved items instead of `list[Item]`.
The report pushes the job of checking test coverage onto the developer instead of doing it.
b_issues: Adds an `Item` import to checkout.py purely for type hints, which is minor.
The `_subtotal_and_tax` docstring describes the rounding rule but not the return value.

verdict.rationale: Both refactors keep the original order of side effects, the error messages, the statuses and the exception chaining, so behavior is preserved in both. A also adds nine characterization tests, run against the old code first, that pin branches the existing suite skipped: VIP stacking on a coupon, the free-shipping threshold, half-up per-line tax rounding, the default tax rate, invalid coupons without side effects, partial reservation rollback, and receipt failure. B relies only on the existing tests for a production refactor and admits it never checked their coverage, leaving that to the developer.
a_issues: Adds an `Item` import only for type hints (harmless).
Splitting `_release` out as a separate helper is a slight extra layer for a two-line loop.
b_issues: No new tests, so key branches stay unprotected during a production refactor: VIP discount, free-shipping threshold, invalid coupon, partial rollback, receipt failure and rounding.
The report admits the existing tests' coverage was never checked and pushes that check onto the developer.
The `_charge` signature is a single overly long line, and it uses a bare `list` type instead of `list[Item]`.
Moves `process_order` to the bottom of the module, which enlarges the diff and makes the entry point harder to find.
